title: The Mirror Arcade
summary: Light a wall with a flame, race a toy car to a catch-bar, fit a selfie to a ring and fire a laser off a turning mirror.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 9.2, Reflection of light by spherical mirrors
concepts: Finding the focal length from one image
Magnification and real or virtual images
Object inside the focus of a concave mirror
learningOutcome: The student can find a mirror’s focal length from one image, place and size images with 1/v + 1/u = 1/f and m = −v/u, and knows a plane mirror turned by θ turns the ray by 2θ.

levels.title: Flicker lights the wall
levels.adds: Baseline: one flash gives u and v, so the focal length follows; then place the object so the real image lands on the wall (Ex 9.1).
hints: A flash tells you u (where Flicker stands) and v (where the image lands). Use the mirror equation 1/v + 1/u = 1/f in magnitudes: f = uv/(u + v).
Now ask for the image at the wall: 1/u = 1/f − 1/v for a real image, in magnitudes.
A real image is in front of the mirror, so a wall can catch it; a virtual one is behind.

levels.title: Dash and the catch-bar
levels.adds: New idea: a convex mirror (f > 0) gives a virtual, upright, smaller image behind it; place the bar where it will be at the line (Ex 9.2, Example 9.4).
hints: Convex mirror: f is positive and u is negative. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
v is positive, so the image is behind the mirror, between the pole and the focus.
Use the distance of the finish line as u, not Dash’s starting distance.

levels.title: The selfie ring
levels.adds: New idea: inside the focus a concave mirror gives an upright, enlarged image, and m = f/(f − u) steepens near the focus (Ex 9.15d, Example 9.3).
hints: For an object inside the focus the image is virtual, upright and larger.
With f = −F and u = −d: m = F/(F − d). Make m equal the ring’s multiple.
Solve for d: d = F(1 − 1/m). The answer is smaller than F.

levels.title: The laser gallery
levels.adds: New idea: when a plane mirror turns by θ the reflected ray turns by 2θ, so the spot moves L tan 2θ along the wall (Ex 9.30).
hints: Compare the ray before and after the turn: the angle of incidence changes by θ, and so does the angle of reflection.
The reflected ray turns through 2θ, twice the dial angle.
tan 2θ = (height of the target) / (distance to the wall). Halve the angle you find.

misconceptions: A convex mirror can form a real image on a screen
A plane mirror turned by θ turns the reflected ray by θ
An object closer than the focus of a concave mirror gives an upside-down image
